findings.title: Cache not re-checked after taking the write lock
findings.body:
`GetWebAssets` checks the cache under `RLock`, releases it, then takes the exclusive `Lock`. Once it holds the exclusive lock it never checks again whether another goroutine has already filled `entryPointAssetsCache`.

Outside dev mode, many requests can arrive while the cache is still nil (cold start, or after a failed load that cached nil). All of them queue on the write lock. Each one then re-opens and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` (or would re-fetch from the CDN), one after another, instead of using the value the first holder just stored.

The standard double-checked pattern fixes this: after `Lock()`, do `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Alternatively, use `sync.Once` for the non-dev path.

findings.title: No regression test for the data race being fixed
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the package-level `entryPointAssetsCache`, but adds no test that would catch it coming back. A small test that calls `GetWebAssets` from several goroutines against a temp `StaticRootPath` containing a valid `build/assets-manifest.json`, run under `go test -race`, would verify the fix and guard against regressions.
